pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Black Sigatoka, caused by the fungus Mycosphaerella fijiensis, is more destructive and causes significant amount of banana yield loss.

type_of_disease.quote: Sigatoka is one of the most prominent fungal diseases that affects banana plants

affected_parts.quote: Black Sigatoka mainly infects banana leaves.

summary.value: Small, dark brown to black spots appear on banana leaves; leaves gradually turn yellow and eventually die as the spots enlarge and coalesce.
summary.quote: The symptom is characterized by the appearance of small, dark brown to black spots on the leaves. Leaves gradually turn yellow and eventually die as these spots enlarge and coalesce.

diagnostic_features.value: Small, dark brown to black spots on the leaves that enlarge and coalesce, causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
diagnostic_features.quote: The symptom is characterized by the appearance of small, dark brown to black spots on the leaves. Leaves gradually turn yellow and eventually die as these spots enlarge and coalesce.

look_alikes.quote: There are two types of Sigatoka: Black Sigatoka and Yellow Sigatoka.

type_of_disease.quote: Inhibitory influence of biocontrol agents, plant oils and an inorganic salt on Mycosphaerella fijiensis and Cordana musae

affected_parts.quote: The infection, which occurs in perianth, spreads to fingers causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of the tissues.

summary.value: Infection spreads from the perianth to the fingers, causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of tissues, with affected tissues corrugated and covered with powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end.
summary.quote: The infection, which occurs in perianth, spreads to fingers causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of the tissues. The affected tissues are corrugated and covered with conidiophores and powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end.

diagnostic_features.value: Affected tissues are corrugated and covered with conidiophores and powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end; dry rot also occurs in the pulp and the affected tissues become dry and fibrous.
diagnostic_features.quote: The affected tissues are corrugated and covered with conidiophores and powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end. Dry rot also occurs in the pulp and the affected tissues become dry and fibrous.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: C. musae is the most common species associated with anthracnose of banana and has been widely accepted as the causal agent of the disease

type_of_disease.quote: Fungal pathogens associated with banana fruits in Sri Lanka and their treatment with essential oils.

affected_parts.quote: Besides causing anthracnose on banana fruits, C. musae can also infect the bracts, flowers, petioles and leaves of banana plants

summary.value: Anthracnose appears as black and sunken lesions on banana fruits, with spore masses or acervuli visible in the lesions; infection often remains quiescent until the fruit ripens and symptoms manifest during storage and marketing.
summary.quote: Symptoms of anthracnose include black and sunken lesions with spore masses or acervuli in the lesion. Infection on the banana usually starts during the development of the fruit but remains quiescent until the fruit ripens; symptoms often manifest during storage and marketing

diagnostic_features.value: Black and sunken lesions with spore masses or acervuli in the lesion; severity increases when fruits are wounded by scratches during handling and transportation.
diagnostic_features.quote: Symptoms of anthracnose include black and sunken lesions with spore masses or acervuli in the lesion... Anthracnose becomes severe when the banana fruits are wounded by scratches during handling and transportation, making the fruit unmarketable.

type_of_disease.quote: This suggests that the fungus is a weak pathogen and needs a wound to infect.

affected_parts.quote: The spots are oval to diamond-shaped, up to 10 cm long, and at right angles to the length of the leaf

summary.value: Oval to diamond-shaped spots up to 10 cm long at right angles to the leaf length, brown on the upper surface with yellow margins and grey to brown below, often merging at leaf margins to form a band of dead tissue with a zigzag yellow border.
summary.quote: The spots are oval to diamond-shaped, up to 10 cm long, and at right angles to the length of the leaf. They are brown on the upper surface, zoned, with yellow margins, and grey to brown below. The spots often merge, covering large areas of the leaf; this occurs particularly at the margin of the leaf giving a band of dead tissue with a zigzag yellow border between diseased and healthy parts.

diagnostic_features.value: Diamond-shaped brown spots with a yellow border, often at the leaf margin; spots are frequently centred on the star-shaped spots of Phyllachora (banana black cross); undersides appear greyish-brown and hairy due to spore production. Lesions caused by C. musae are generally larger and more elongated compared to C. johnstonii.
diagnostic_features.quote: Look for the diamond-shaped brown spots, with a yellow border, often common along the margin of the leaf. Look to see if the spots are centred on the star-shaped spots of Phyllachora .

look_alikes.quote: Association of diamond leaf spot, Cordana musae, with leaf spots of banana black cross, Phyllachora musicola... Another species, Cordana johnsonii , occurs in Australia and Tonga.

conflicts.alternative_value: Cordana musae; Cordana johnstonii (also known as Neocordana musae and Neocordana johnstonii)
conflicts.note: Bayer source reports two causal species (C. musae and C. johnstonii) and notes synonymy with Neocordana; Lucid fact sheet lists only C. musae as scientific name.
Bayer source uses the name 'Cordana leaf spot' as primary name; Lucid fact sheet uses 'Banana diamond leaf spot' and 'Banana (Cordana) leaf spot'.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Pestalotiopsis palmara is the primary, but not the only, Pestalotiopsis species associated with palms.

type_of_disease.quote: The fungus Pestalotiopsis causes leaf spots, petiole/rachis blights and sometimes a bud rot of palms.

affected_parts.quote: Pestalotiopsis is a fungus that causes diseases of both the palm leaf petiole and leaf blade, often at the same time... where it can cause a fatal bud rot.

summary.value: Leaf spots begin as very small yellow, brown or black spots that enlarge, usually turning gray with a black outline; similar lesions occur on the petiole and rachis, and lesions may coalesce into leaf or rachis blight, sometimes progressing to a fatal bud rot.
summary.quote: Leaf spots will begin as very small, yellow, brown or black spots that enlarge in size. The spot usually turns gray with a black outline. Lesions on the petiole and rachis are similar.

diagnostic_features.value: Spots that turn a grayish color outlined in black; unlike other leaf spot and petiole blight pathogens, Pestalotiopsis attacks all parts of the leaf from base to tip (leaf blade, petiole, rachis, and even leaf spines), and on Phoenix roebelenii may progress to a fatal bud rot.
diagnostic_features.quote: Often, the spots turn a grayish color that are outlined in black... unlike the other leaf spot and petiole blight pathogens, which attack either the leaf blade or the leaf petiole, Pestalotiopsis attacks all parts of the leaf from base to tip.

value: Leaf Spots and Leaf Blights of Palm
look_alikes.quote: For information on other leaf spots and petiole/rachis blights, refer to the following documents: Leaf Spots and Leaf Blights of Palm at https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pp142 ; Petiole/Rachis Blight of Palm at https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pp145 ; and Calonectria (Cylindrocladium) Leaf Spot of Palm at ( https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pp302 ).

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The virus that causes the bunchy top belongs to the family of Nanoviridae, genus Babuvirus

type_of_disease.quote: The virus that causes the bunchy top belongs to the family of Nanoviridae, genus Babuvirus

affected_parts.quote: The first symptoms appear as streaks and dark green dots of variable lengths in leaves and petioles. Later, leaves develop a marginal chlorosis, their development is reduced, they become stunted and erect

summary.value: Streaks and dark green dots of variable lengths in leaves and petioles; later leaves develop marginal chlorosis, become stunted and erect, appearing to present offsetting in the higher parts of the plant giving a 'bunchy top' appearance.
summary.quote: The first symptoms appear as streaks and dark green dots of variable lengths in leaves and petioles. Later, leaves develop a marginal chlorosis, their development is reduced, they become stunted and erect, appearing to present offsetting in the higher parts of the plant. This symptom gives it the name of "bunchy top"

diagnostic_features.value: Stunted and erect leaves with marginal chlorosis giving the plant a characteristic 'bunchy top' appearance at the higher parts of the plant.
diagnostic_features.quote: they become stunted and erect, appearing to present offsetting in the higher parts of the plant. This symptom gives it the name of "bunchy top"
